modules.name: Sync-conflict review panel
modules.purpose: Make automatic conflict resolution reviewable without ever making it blocking, and prevent a clock-skewed write from silently winning.

modules.name: Standard reports and Custom Report Builder
modules.purpose: Render and deliver the platform's five standard report data sets, and let tenants shape those sets into saved formats.

modules.name: Shift handoff panel
modules.purpose: Carry the truth of one shift into the next as a produced artefact read, acknowledged and annotated where the incoming supervisor will work.

modules.name: Operational actions, the closed set of ten
modules.purpose: Give shift authorities the small set of light operational powers a control room needs without eroding the Command Center authoring/ownership boundary.

modules.name: Identity, Authentication and Device Mode
modules.purpose: Establish and maintain a trustworthy, attributable identity on the device, because attribution, qualification, language and security key off who is logged in.

modules.name: My Runs
modules.purpose: Present, honestly and without allocation, the work assigned to the logged-in identity, and be the single list the worker manages.

modules.name: Run Player
modules.purpose: Be the dominant surface and the engine that renders the Workflow package, driving the worker forward through Studio-authored screens.

modules.name: Data Capture and Evidence
modules.purpose: Be where the application earns its less-error-prone-than-paper claim and where the platform's evidence integrity is established at source.

modules.name: On-Device Detection and Containment
modules.purpose: Make the platform's quality guarantees local, uniform, and beyond the reach of configuration, running gates, detection, classification, hold and containment on-device offline.

modules.name: Offline and Sync Engine
modules.purpose: Be what lets the safety backbone and the capture model work on a floor with no reliable connectivity.

modules.name: Security and Data Protection
modules.purpose: Application-managed encrypted store, remote wipe with final-sync attempt, PIN lockout, suspension states, minimal on-device scope.

modules.name: Coaching Rendering
modules.purpose: Prevention Agent cards, replay, dismissal, per-language content, authored-instruction fallback offline.

modules.name: Gates and Sign-Off Authority
modules.purpose: Qualification-gate posture, clearance delivery, the parked Run, substitute sign-off, step-level re-confirmation.

modules.name: Notifications
modules.purpose: Identity-scoped in-application inbox, no operating-system push at launch, two-tier work-instruction change notices.

modules.name: Worker Lifecycle on Device
modules.purpose: Pause, step-away and hand-back, substitution handover, at-step certification-expiry enforcement.

modules.name: Training Library Viewer
modules.purpose: Online-only viewer of versioned, per-language training material; no production records.

business_rules.statement: Conflict resolution is automatic: the most recent write wins, by the device-side timestamp, and the full conflict event is audited. The panel is a review instrument, never a blocker — work never stops waiting on conflict review.

Where a device's clock deviates from server receipt beyond the tenant's clock-skew threshold, the platform orders that write by server-receipt time instead, flags it as skew-affected, and a skew-flagged write cannot win a conflict unreviewed.
Resolve All excludes skew-flagged conflicts, enforced at the service.
Resolve All is all-or-nothing; no partial bulk resolution occurs.
Flagging a wrong resolution opens the append-only correction path and does not alter the sync result.

A conflict whose two values disagree beyond the screen's specification limits is passed to the rule-based deviation mechanism for evaluation, because two materially different readings of the same capture is a quality event.
Exactly five standard data sets exist; no interface path creates a sixth.
Every rendered report and every delivered file carries a data-as-of timestamp.
Job Type is available as a first-class filter and no Service Type tag drives any behaviour.
No outbound integration path into tenant-external systems exists on this surface.
Materiality follows the platform default — any change to a severity count.
No shift is blocked from starting by an unacknowledged brief, under any configuration.
No brief is back-filled after a missed shift.
Exactly ten operational actions are reachable from this surface; no eleventh endpoint exists.
Every action executes through the same owning Delivery Operations Hub service that the Delivery Operations Hub's own screen for that record uses, verified by contract test.
Every action writes exactly one audit entry in the same transaction as its change.
Lot release is Quality Manager only, uniformly, with no exception by work type, risk class or tag.
A Supervisor's clearance grant is limited to an expired qualification; a never-held qualification requires a Quality Manager.
No path exists to override a specification gate or the evaluation gate, pause or stop a run, edit a record or configuration, or create a Job or run.
No action is queued client-side under any connectivity condition.
No operational record exists anywhere in the platform that was not created by a capture event originating in this surface.
The deterministic safety layer executes with the network interface disabled, producing identical gate, detection, and classification outcomes to the connected case.
No screen in any module, in any state, in any release of this scope displays a pace figure, a countdown against expectation, or a comparison to another worker.

Principle 3 — append, never overwrite, after commit: the on-device store has no update path for a committed capture, only an insert path for an annotation record; enforced at the storage schema, not the application layer.
Principle 2 — the login is the credential: no permission, qualification, language, or assignment may ever be resolved from the device record. Device identity is provenance, never authority.
The capture record and its local audit entry commit in one local transaction; a failure of either aborts both. An action that cannot be audited does not happen.
The device accepts exactly five command classes and rejects any other class with a typed reason.
No surface represents a command as effective on a device before that device has acknowledged application.
Command application is idempotent — applying the same command twice produces the same end state as applying it once.
No surface renders a hold as globally released; hold state is rendered per device.
The application exposes exactly six destinations and no seventh.
Maximum navigation depth from Login to any screen is three actions.
No pattern discards, overwrites, or silently drops captured data, in any branch.
A second-identity step-up preserves the worker's session, binds the authorising identity to exactly one authorisation, and releases it immediately afterwards.
A designated high-risk action requiring a forced sync does not proceed when the sync cannot complete.
Offline login succeeds within the tenant-set trust window and fails cleanly outside it, with the ceiling of 72 hours never exceeded by any tenant setting.
A Run whose package has not arrived is shown as not-yet-ready with a reason, is not enterable, and is never omitted from the list.
One rendered screen produces exactly one Step Execution record.
An in-flight Run is never re-based onto a new workflow version.
The application renders exactly the seven capture types of the adopted DEC-CAP-001 contract plus none for instruction-only screens, and renders no eighth type.
No captured media is reachable from the device gallery, any file browser, or any other application.
Named-location provenance is recorded as a named place with no coordinate, is disclosed to the worker, and never blocks a capture.
Media is evicted only after confirmed server receipt plus an integrity check.
A Severity 1 classification places a local hold within the same local transaction as the capture that triggered it.
The hold lands on the Lot where one exists, otherwise the Unit for serialized work, otherwise the Run.
No tenant configuration can weaken any element of the deterministic layer, and the platform rejects a looser-than-floor value rather than logging it.
No artificial-intelligence component appears anywhere in the detection or classification code path.

Reconnection ordering follows the adopted DEC-SYNC-001 position: the stop class applies before any capture leaves the device, the full capture queue then drains, and the enabling class applies only afterwards.
The worker is never presented with a conflict, a queue editor, or a sync obligation.

The Severity 1 floor is platform-fixed — automatic freeze plus Quality-Manager-only release plus escalation — and no tenant configuration and no notification failure can weaken it. A notification is never the only mechanism enforcing the hold.

The Command Center is the cockpit, never the engine: every action is a command against a Delivery Operations Hub-owned record, executed through the owning Delivery Operations Hub service, written to the Delivery Operations Hub audit trail.

decisions.question: What is the conflict list cap's value, how does a reviewer reach conflicts beyond it, and what does Resolve All do about them?
options: (a) state the cap value and provide paging so every conflict is reachable, with Resolve All acting on the current page only and saying so
(b) state the cap value and have Resolve All act on every ordinary conflict regardless of listing, with a confirmation stating the true count
(c) make the cap a tenant setting above a platform floor
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required; recommendation option (a)
decisions.impact: A Resolve All that silently omits conflicts leaves unreviewed automatic resolutions with no route to them.

decisions.question: What are the exact identities of the five standard report data sets, and is set 4 'Clearance (qualification-override) frequency by role' or 'Override frequency by role'?
options: (a) adopt reading A and rename consistently across both Parts
(b) adopt reading B and define its population explicitly, enumerating what counts as an override
(c) replace the set entirely with an outcome-flavoured set, provided the list stays at five
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required; recommendation option (a); blueprint implements neither name as final
decisions.impact: The set's population, and therefore every number in it.

decisions.question: What does 'and above' / 'Supervisor+' / 'QM+' enumerate across five additive, non-hierarchical roles?
options: Enumeration of specific grants
Inference from a rank ordering
decisions.adopted_working_position: Read 'Supervisor and above' as 'any identity holding the Supervisor role or the Quality Manager role', and never as a rank comparison; 'Quality Manager and above' means the Quality Manager grant only.
decisions.status: Pre-existing — open (Client Decision Required)
decisions.impact: Every permission matrix cell in the chapter.

decisions.question: Does the Plant Manager persona hold decision authority, or only read-and-escalate?
options: Read-and-escalate unless the Quality Manager role is also held
decisions.adopted_working_position: The Plant Manager's scope across every row is read-and-escalate unless the Quality Manager role is also held.
decisions.status: Pre-existing — open (Client Decision Required)
decisions.impact: Plant Manager users may expect decision authority they do not hold.

decisions.question: Is the closed set of ten complete, given surface-originating writes that sit outside it?
options: Restate the closed set to include them
Keep the set as operational actions only
decisions.status: New, raised here — Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Writes outside the ten erode the scope promise of the closed action set.

decisions.question: On reconnection, does a device upload pending captures before or after pulling pending commands?
options: (a) commands first, unconditionally
(b) captures first, unconditionally
(c) a hybrid keyed on a pending destructive command / class-based split
(d) interleaved application after the drain
decisions.adopted_working_position: Stop-class commands first — suspension in all three states, device de-authorisation and remote wipe, and any tenant compliance stop — then the full capture upload with nothing discarded, then the enabling-class commands (lot release, reassignment or substitution, qualification clearance, version change). Adopted 2026-08-14 at Option C.
decisions.status: adopted working position; client ratification outstanding
decisions.impact: Determines whether a suspension lands before more work is created or evidence is at risk.

decisions.question: How long may a wipe command remain pending, and what happens if the device never returns?
decisions.status: Pre-existing — open (Client Decision Required)
decisions.impact: A hold can appear propagating indefinitely; unsynced work preserved on a device that never returns.

decisions.question: What happens when notification routing resolves to nobody holding the target role on shift?
options: Platform default escalates to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery
decisions.status: Pre-existing — open (Client Decision Required)
decisions.impact: Escalation delivery when no on-shift holder exists.

decisions.question: Is the Prevention Agent gated by authoring-time policy only, or does every action agent route through a runtime human gate?
options: §3.7/§6.6.1 — operates entirely under pre-authorised Studio-authored policy, runtime gate only for proposals beyond it
§8.3.2/§8.3.3 — every action agent routes through a human gate before any effect; Prevention Agent labelled 'action, gated'
decisions.adopted_working_position: Gating declared per agent in the agent record's governance-binding field; the Prevention Agent carries 'authoring-time policy' with no per-event runtime gate; the Deviation and Containment Agent carries 'runtime human gate' for proposals beyond pre-authorised containment. Adopted 2026-08-14.
decisions.status: adopted working position; client ratification outstanding
decisions.impact: Whether an agent's containment proposals require a per-event human gate.

decisions.question: May an approved Lane B proposal auto-publish a patch with no second approval, against the three-stage Author/Reviewer/Release Authority chain?
options: §5.11.1 — explicit human sign-off at each of Author, Reviewer, Release Authority
§5.16.3/§6.7.4 — approved Lane B proposal auto-publishes a patch with no second approval
decisions.status: Pre-existing — open (Client Decision Required)
decisions.impact: A Lane B change could reach devices with one human signature rather than three.

decisions.question: Which fields are package-borne versus server-only? §6.7.4 says Part VII holds the contract; Part VII does not enumerate it.
decisions.status: Pre-existing — open (Client Decision Required)
decisions.impact: Determines what the offline device can enforce without a server.

decisions.question: Is the per-tenant refresh floor a strictness ceiling?
decisions.status: New, raised in chapter 21 — Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Board refresh interval bounds.

decisions.question: What is the behaviour when the Client Command Center surface itself loses connectivity?
options: Freeze-and-label with disabled controls and no client-side queue
decisions.status: New, raised in chapter 21 — Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: A user could believe an action was taken when the session was frozen.

decisions.question: What are the browser support, viewport and session-timeout rules for the Client Command Center?
options: A tenant setting above a platform floor
decisions.status: New, raised in chapter 21 — Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: A decision-capable session left open on a shared plant tablet.

decisions.question: Is the hub named 'Delivery Operations Hub' or 'Digital Operations Hub'?
options: Delivery Operations Hub (Statement of Work §1.2, Part IV heading)
Digital Operations Hub (blueprint commission alternative)
decisions.status: Pre-existing — open (Client Decision Required)
decisions.impact: Naming divergence; not silently reconciled.

decisions.question: Does a Job carry a single Area binding (hard constraint, §4.5.1) or one parent node at the tenant's configured depth (§2.1)?
options: §2.1 — 'one parent node per Job' at the tenant's configured depth
§4.5.1 — a Job carries a single Area binding; one Area per Job is a hard constraint
decisions.adopted_working_position: A Job anchors at the deepest parent node its tenant configured, so the provenance stamp resolves site, line and cell down to that node.
decisions.status: adopted working position; client ratification outstanding
decisions.impact: Named-location provenance resolution on every capture.

decisions.question: Is the Site level a required minimum (mandatory per §4.3.1) or open (§2.1)?
options: §2.1 — marked open
§4.3.1 — stated as mandatory
decisions.adopted_working_position: The Site level is mandatory with a default Site auto-created at tenant provisioning, so the site element of the provenance stamp is always resolvable.
decisions.status: adopted working position; client ratification outstanding
decisions.impact: Whether the site element of provenance is always resolvable.

decisions.question: Which compliance standards mandate deletion?
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Data-lifecycle and deletion obligations.

decisions.question: Which certifications apply (nothing ITAR-flavoured is committed before it lands)?
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Compliance posture commitments.

decisions.question: Which seven capture types make up the contract — the §7.8.3/§1.7 set or the §5.5.3 Part V set?
options: §7.8.3 and §1.7: measurement, scan, photo, checklist, boolean, electronic signature or acknowledgement, free text
§5.5.3 Part V: measurement entry, photo capture, barcode or Quick Response code scan, checkbox confirmation, digital signature, free text, dropdown selection
decisions.adopted_working_position: The Part V set of seven: measurement entry, photo capture, barcode or Quick Response code scan, checkbox confirmation, digital signature, free text, and dropdown selection, plus none for instruction-only screens.
decisions.status: adopted working position; ratification with the client, jointly across Studio and Frontline workstreams
decisions.impact: Determines what an author can build and what a worker can be asked to do.

decisions.question: Does the package carry all three work-instruction difficulty levels or only the assigned worker's level?
options: All levels
Only the assigned worker's level
decisions.adopted_working_position: Until it resolves, the package definition carries all levels.
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Package size and offline rendering of the correct instruction level.

decisions.question: What is the device behaviour when on-device storage is exhausted?
options: (a) block new capture with a clear message and force a sync
(b) block new media capture only while permitting non-media captures
(c) refuse to start additional Runs while permitting completion of Runs in progress
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required; recommendation is a combination of (b) and (c) with (a) as the terminal state
decisions.impact: Refusing captures stops the line; evicting unconfirmed data destroys evidence.

decisions.question: Which scanner hardware families must be supported?
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Reliability of the fast scan path on day one.

decisions.question: What happens when the parked Run is the worker's only assigned Run?
decisions.status: Not specified in the Statement of Work — proposed as new
decisions.impact: A worker with a single parked Run has nothing to continue with.

decisions.question: Does a library-pointer edit propagate into an in-flight run's containment checklist or coaching asset despite version pinning?
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Version pinning integrity for library-referenced content.

decisions.question: Record-finish window default and bounds.
decisions.status: Pre-existing — open
decisions.impact: 48 hours default, floor 24 hours, ceiling 7 days.

contradictions.description: Report set 4 is named 'Clearance (qualification-override) frequency by role' in the Delivery Operations Hub Part and 'Override frequency by role' in this Part; the set's population differs.
The conflict list is 'capped' with a total count and Resolve All accepts every listed ordinary conflict, but the cap value, paging, and Resolve All scope beyond the cap are unstated.
conflicting_values: Resolve All acts on the visible page only
Resolve All acts on every ordinary conflict regardless of listing

contradictions.description: The set of Command Center actions is closed at ten as operational actions, yet several writes originate on the surface outside it — report-format authoring, manual close of a stuck run, prior-case relevance marks, one-tap agent feedback.
conflicting_values: Closed set of ten operational actions
Additional surface-originating writes outside the ten

contradictions.description: The Statement of Work never fixes whether a reconnecting device uploads pending captures before or after pulling pending commands; safety argues commands first, data integrity argues captures first.

§2.1 states the superseded 'one Area per Job' constraint becomes 'one parent node per Job' at the tenant's configured depth, while §4.5.1 states a Job carries a single Area binding and one Area per Job is a hard constraint.
conflicting_values: one parent node per Job at the tenant's configured depth (§2.1)
one Area per Job as a hard constraint (§4.5.1)

contradictions.description: Whether the Site level is a required minimum is marked open in §2.1 and stated as mandatory in §4.3.1.
Both sources say the capture-type contract has seven types, but the sets differ: the Studio set adds dropdown selection and merges checklist and boolean into one checkbox confirmation.
conflicting_values: §7.8.3 and §1.7: measurement, scan, photo, checklist, boolean, electronic signature or acknowledgement, free text
§5.5.3: measurement entry, photo capture, barcode or QR scan, checkbox confirmation, digital signature, free text, dropdown selection

contradictions.description: §3.7 and §6.6.1 say the Prevention Agent operates entirely under pre-authorised Studio-authored policy with a runtime gate only for proposals beyond it, while §8.3.2 says every action agent routes through a human gate before any effect and §8.3.3 labels it 'action, gated'.
conflicting_values: authoring-time policy, no per-event runtime gate
every action agent routes through a runtime human gate

contradictions.description: §5.11.1 requires explicit human sign-off at each of Author, Reviewer, and Release Authority before any Workflow content reaches the frontline, while §5.16.3 and §6.7.4 have an approved Lane B proposal auto-publish a patch with no second approval.
conflicting_values: Lane B auto-publish with no second approval

contradictions.description: The blueprint commission's alternative name 'Digital Operations Hub' diverges from the Statement of Work's 'Delivery Operations Hub' (§1.2, Part IV heading).
§6.7.4 states the authoritative field-by-field assignment of package-borne versus server-only values lives in Part VII's package contract, but Part VII does not enumerate it.
conflicting_values: Part VII does not enumerate it

contradictions.description: Whether a library-pointer edit propagates into an in-flight run's containment checklist or coaching asset despite version pinning is unresolved.

The 30-minute Shift Handoff Agent run time before shift end and the 30-minute unacknowledged-brief grace period share a value but are a coincidence of values, configured separately, not a shared mechanism.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Client Command Center session loses connectivity
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Panel freezes and every resolution control is disabled; nothing is queued
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Session remains offline
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Automatic resolutions stand unreviewed; work never stopped
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Reconnection and refresh

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Resolution write fails during Resolve All / any Command Center action's service call fails
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Nothing is resolved; all-or-nothing; control returns to pre-action state with the service named and time of attempt; one deliberate retry offered
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The service remains unavailable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The action did not happen, the user has been told, and the alternate route on the Delivery Operations Hub's own screens is named; for action 4 containment persists
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Deliberate re-issue; nothing replays

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Panel staleness / stale underlying reads
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Freshness marking and as-of stamps
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Content remains stale
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Explicit stale rendering with age
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Refresh on reconnection

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Conflict-event transport loss
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Panel refreshes at next successful poll
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Transport remains down
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Automatic resolutions stand
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Transport restoration

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Report generation or delivery failure
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: No partial file produced or offered; explicit failure naming the data set and the as-of time attempted
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Repeated generation failure across a scheduled window
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No file delivered, delivery recorded as failed, recipient set notified in-app
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The next scheduled run generates normally

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The Shift Handoff Agent does not produce a brief
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Panel states plainly that no brief was produced for the named shift and that platform operations has been notified
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A second consecutive failure, or a failure outlasting a shift
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The shift starts without a brief; persistent degradation escalates to the Plant Manager view
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The agent resumes on its next timer; no brief is back-filled

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Actions 4, 8 and 10 where the effect must reach a device
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Honest per-device command state rendering
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Device never returns
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Pre-command state preserved; hold remains in force
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Device sync

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Authorisation failure on a Command Center action
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Refused at the service and audited as a denial
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: n/a
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Action did not occur
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Correct grant

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Actions 2 and 3 where the item's context is incomplete
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Queue fallback then FB-CC-WRITE
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Context remains incomplete
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Decision not taken
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Context restoration

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Connectivity loss during normal execution
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Continue fully offline from the pinned package with the durable queue accumulating
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Offline trust window expires — FB-FL-AUTH-01 takes over
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The worker completes assigned Runs offline and the device holds all data
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Automatic resumption; server folds late captures in flagged late_arrival

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Authentication or authority data cannot be refreshed
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Operate on cached credentials and qualifications within the tenant-set offline trust window, default about 24 hours, ceiling 72 hours
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: On window expiry no new session may start and no high-risk action may proceed; an in-progress step is not yanked away
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No session, all local data preserved, device usable only to display the honest state
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Reconnection and refresh

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Work package missing, incomplete, or failing integrity verification
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Present the Run honestly as not-yet-ready and retry the download when connectivity permits
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No assigned Run is ready; Supervisor signalled through run no-show at plus 15 minutes with auto-cancel at plus 30
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The Run is never partially rendered and never started against an unverified package
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Successful package delivery and verification

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A capture cannot be committed locally
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry the local transaction once, then twice, with the value preserved on screen and un-committed
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Storage exhaustion — FB-FL-STORE-01 applies
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A blocked step with an un-committed value visible; no partial record, no phantom capture
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Storage remediation or device substitution

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Upload of a committed capture or evidence object fails
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Resume from the interruption point rather than restarting
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: After a bounded number of failures the item moves to a local dead-letter holding area and is surfaced to the Client Command Center
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The item is retained on the device and never deleted; media evicted only after confirmed server receipt plus an integrity check
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Server-side remediation and requeue; Recovery Point Objective zero for committed captures

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A command cannot be downloaded, validated, or applied
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Reject with a typed reason and acknowledge the rejection
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Unacknowledged command aging past a tenant-visible threshold surfaces as propagation lag
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Pre-command state preserved; holds stay in force rather than lifting on an unvalidated release
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Next sync; command ledger reconciled against device acknowledgements

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The agentic and reasoning layer is unavailable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The step's authored Work Instructions, which travel inside the Workflow package
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not applicable — the authored instructions are part of the pinned package
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Full execution continues with authored guidance only; deterministic layer untouched
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Agent availability restored; resume is a separate audited act after an emergency pause

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A qualification gate blocks a step
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Lenient posture notifies without blocking; strict posture (the platform default) hard-blocks
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Offline, the blocked Run parks and the worker continues with their other assigned Runs
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The parked Run, with all prior captures preserved and queued. There is no on-device worker override, ever.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Clearance arrival (Client Command Center action 10) or certification correction

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A Severity 1 classification occurs and escalation cannot be delivered
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The hold and containment are unaffected, because they are local; escalation queues durably
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No holder of the target role on shift — platform default escalates to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery (DEC-NOSHIFT-001)
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The breaching lot, unit, or run is frozen locally, and only a Quality Manager can release it, through a lot-release command
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Quality Manager release; propagation lag recorded as telemetry

failures_fallbacks.trigger: On-device storage is exhausted
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Not specified in the Statement of Work — DEC-STORE-001
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Open
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Capture blocked with all existing data preserved; never eviction of unconfirmed evidence
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Storage remediation; behaviour to be defined per platform in the Frontline Functional Specification

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Clock skew beyond the tenant threshold (default about 5 minutes, ceiling 60 minutes)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Flag as an operational event so a materially wrong clock is visible rather than silently trusted
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A conflict that would otherwise resolve by device timestamp routes to the Client Command Center's conflict-and-skew review
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The record is preserved with both timestamps and the skew flag; nothing discarded and nothing silently corrected
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Clock correction, typically by the device's own time synchronisation

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Security event: suspension, de-authorisation, remote wipe, or lockout
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Soft: master-data writes blocked platform-side, operations continue. Hard: no new Runs start, in-flight Runs complete. Compliance: immediate lock, all local data preserved, fixed message shown.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: An offline device cannot perform the final sync before wipe; DEC-WIPE-001 open
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Locked device with local data preserved and no further capture possible
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Reinstatement, credential reset, or device replacement

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A screen element cannot be rendered
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Package-level rejection at delivery, before the Run is offered as ready
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Mid-Run failure — the player stops at the affected step rather than skipping it, preserves all prior captures, and marks the Run blocked
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A blocked Run with complete, immutable prior captures; never a skipped gated step
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Content correction, republication, and a new assignment

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Scanner hardware fails or a code will not read
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Camera-based scanning
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Manual entry of the identifier where the authored screen permits it; otherwise the step is blocked
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A blocked step with no fabricated identity; the platform never invents a unit identifier
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Relabelling, lighting, or scanner replacement; DEC-SCAN-001 open for the hardware list

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Chapter-level failure: loss of the execution surface itself — the application will not start, or the device is unusable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: A conformant substitute device — the login is the credential, so identity, qualifications, language and attribution follow the worker
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The tenant's own paper or method of record for the affected Run, executed outside the platform (Recommendation — R&D; no SoW procedure exists)
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A controlled stop of the affected Run with all locally committed data preserved on the original device pending recovery — never a silent continuation and never a discard
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Device replacement plus sync of the original device when serviceable
